nsa_5g_downgrade_risk.explanation: Primary backup USID_27 has 8 5G cells — more than USID_00's 6 — so users anchored on NR at USID_00 can maintain 5G service on USID_27. All five backup USIDs carry at least 2 5G cells (USID_41 minimum), so no wholesale 5G-to-4G downgrade scenario exists for any segment of USID_00's dominant area.

capacity_verdict_reasoning: USID_27 (23.4), USID_29 (25.6), and USID_37 (25.6) provide high-capacity 5G-dominant backup options; these three alone cover > 100% of USID_00's dominant pixels through overlapping absorption.

Post-outage load factors are all below 0.015 — orders of magnitude below the 0.5 medium-risk threshold — confirming that the capacity of each backup remains virtually unperturbed by USID_00's shutdown.
USID_41's lower score (15.6) is a minor concern in isolation, but its post-outage load factor of 0.012 shows trivial incremental load, so its capacity is not a binding constraint.
5G continuity is ensured across the network — no backup USID drops to 4G-only, preserving NR service for all USID_00 users post-handover.
key_findings_for_stage4: USID_00 is a high-capacity 5G-dominant macro site (capacity_score=25.6); its shutdown removes significant NR capacity from the local cell plan, but backups have equivalent or higher 5G capability.
